# Unit test for function escape
def test_escape():
    import re

    pattern = re.compile(r"\\(\'|\"|\\|[abfnrtv]|x.{0,2}|[0-7]{1,3})")

    def make_match(literal):
        m = pattern.match(literal)
        assert m is not None, "pattern failed to match %r" % literal
        return m

    def expect_value_error(literal):
        try:
            escape(make_match(literal))
        except ValueError:
            return True
        return False

    # Simple single-character escapes
    simple_cases = {
        "a": "\a",
        "b": "\b",
        "f": "\f",
        "n": "\n",
        "r": "\r",
        "t": "\t",
        "v": "\v",
        "'": "'",
        '"': '"',
        "\\": "\\",
    }
    for letter, expected in simple_cases.items():
        result = escape(make_match("\\" + letter))
        assert result == expected, (
            "escape(%r) returned %r, expected %r" % ("\\" + letter, result, expected)
        )

    # Hexadecimal escapes
    assert escape(make_match("\\x41")) == "A"
    assert escape(make_match("\\x61")) == "a"
    assert escape(make_match("\\x30")) == "0"
    assert escape(make_match("\\x00")) == "\x00"
    assert escape(make_match("\\xff")) == "\xff"
    assert escape(make_match("\\x7e")) == "~"

    # Single-digit hex (regex permits 0..2 hex digits; < 2 raises later,
    # but a 2-digit form must decode correctly)
    assert escape(make_match("\\x09")) == "\t"

    # Octal escapes
    assert escape(make_match("\\0")) == "\x00"
    assert escape(make_match("\\7")) == "\x07"
    assert escape(make_match("\\12")) == "\n"          # 0o12 == 10
    assert escape(make_match("\\101")) == "A"          # 0o101 == 65
    assert escape(make_match("\\777")) == chr(0o777)   # 0o777 == 511
    assert escape(make_match("\\176")) == "~"          # 0o176 == 126

    # Only the matched portion is consumed; group(0) includes the backslash
    m = pattern.match("\\nrest-of-text")
    assert m is not None
    assert escape(m) == "\n"

    # Invalid hex escapes raise ValueError
    assert expect_value_error("\\x"), "truncated \\x escape should raise"
    assert expect_value_error("\\xy"), "non-hex digit after \\x should raise"
    assert expect_value_error("\\xzz"), "non-hex digits after \\x should raise"
    assert expect_value_error("\\xg1"), "invalid hex digit should raise"

    # Valid-but-short hex like \\xA handled: len(hexes) < 2 -> error
    assert expect_value_error("\\xa"), "single hex digit should raise"

    # Sanity: results are str instances
    assert isinstance(escape(make_match("\\n")), str)
    assert isinstance(escape(make_match("\\x41")), str)
    assert isinstance(escape(make_match("\\101")), str)

# Unit test for function evalString
def test_evalString():
    import pytest

    # Simple strings with no escapes
    assert evalString("'hello'") == "hello"
    assert evalString('"hello"') == "hello"
    assert evalString("''") == ""
    assert evalString('""') == ""

    # Triple-quoted strings
    assert evalString("'''hello'''") == "hello"
    assert evalString('"""hello"""') == "hello"
    assert evalString("''''''") == ""

    # Simple escape sequences
    assert evalString(r"'\n'") == "\n"
    assert evalString(r"'\t'") == "\t"
    assert evalString(r"'\r'") == "\r"
    assert evalString(r"'\\'") == "\\"
    assert evalString(r"'\a\b\f\v'") == "\a\b\f\v"
    assert evalString(r"'\''") == "'"
    assert evalString(r"'\"'") == '"'
    assert evalString(r"'a\nb'") == "a\nb"

    # Hex escapes
    assert evalString(r"'\x41'") == "A"
    assert evalString(r"'\x4a'") == "j"
    assert evalString(r"'\x00'") == "\x00"
    assert evalString(r"'\xff'") == "\xff"

    # Octal escapes
    assert evalString(r"'\101'") == "A"
    assert evalString(r"'\0'") == "\x00"
    assert evalString(r"'\377'") == "\xff"

    # Mixed escapes
    assert evalString(r"'a\nb\x41\101'") == "a\nbAA"

    # Round-trip: every character 0-255 should survive repr + evalString
    for i in range(256):
        c = chr(i)
        assert evalString(repr(c)) == c, "failed for char %d" % i

    # Invalid hex escapes raise ValueError
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        evalString(r"'\x'")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        evalString(r"'\x4'")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        evalString(r"'\xzz'")

    # Bad quoting raises AssertionError
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        evalString("hello")          # no quotes
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        evalString("'hello\"")       # mismatched quotes
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        evalString("'")              # too short
